1.why: Four distinct transition families (sequence/restatement/contrast/example); 'For instance,' is the most common key type in this option shape.

2.why: 'In some circumstances, however,' is the only elaborated, hedged option among three terse ones — the crafted outlier.

3.why: Contrast and similarity distractors flank a restatement; 'For instance,' is the only exemplification option and the usual key here.

4.why: Only C states a method (satellite images 2000-2020, horizontal distance between successive images); the others give purpose, cause, or a result.

5.why: Only B has the explicit old-versus-new pivot: 'Doctors once blamed ulcers on stress and spicy food, but ... H. pylori causes most of them.'

6.why: Only C generalizes beyond the two cities — a 40-city review with a rate, 'indicating the pattern holds broadly' — which is what a skeptic needs.

7.why: 'Even so,' is the lone contrast among restatement/result/similarity options.

8.why: Contrast, explanation and comparison split the field; 'As a result,' is the plainest causal key and 'After all' rarely keys.

9.why: All four share one sentence frame varying only numbers and condition; 'dense fog' is the harbor-relevant condition that also motivates 'without sun'.

10.why: 'For this reason' and 'Thus' are the same causal family and cancel each other out, leaving 'By contrast' over the restatement.

11.why: 'With few exceptions,' is the elaborated qualifier among three stock one-word transitions.

12.why: Same frame, only cultivar and held-fixed variable vary; 'Salinas' is the canonical lettuce cultivar and temperature the variable most naturally paired with a 50 percent optimum.

13.why: 'Nevertheless,' is the only concessive against similarity/restatement/result.

14.why: Only C joins the example to the named principle — 'illustrate convergent evolution: though separated by over 400 million years, both independently evolved streamlined bodies'.

15.why: Only A puts both figures in one contrastive sentence ('up to 3,000 miles' vs 'as far as 9,000 miles'); the others give one species or no numbers.

16.why: Only A spans the whole arc from closure in 1980 to swimmers returning in 2018; the rest are single facts.

18.why: Only C states the full mechanism and both directions — otters eat urchins, kelp collapsed when otters went, rebounded when they returned.

17.why: 'However,' is the only contrast among result/addition/restatement.

19.why: Only A rebuts the assumption — 'Far from vanishing, Welsh had rebounded to about 540,000 speakers'; the others report decline.

20.why: Fixed frame varying only organism and thickness; blue mussels are the standard dominant fouling organism by weight, with the mid-range 19 mm.

21.why: Same frame varying only the caveat; the absence of an unlit control path is the limitation that most directly blocks crediting the increase to the lighting.

22.why: Only A links all three links of the chain — wolves return, elk avoid valleys, willow and aspen regrow.

23.why: Only A names one cause driving several effects: 'Rising ocean temperatures drove several changes at once'.

24.why: 'That said,' is the only concessive pivot against result/similarity/restatement.
